display_name: British English (incl. UK Gen Z / Roadman)

street.description: London/Manchester roadman / UK Gen Z — heavy MLE (Multicultural London English) markers.

casual_social.description: Default UK B2C social — drier humor, understatement, sarcasm-tolerant.

professional_casual.description: UK LinkedIn — wittier and more self-effacing than US equivalent.

corporate_formal.description: Press, finance, legal — RP-leaning standard British English.

grammar_quirks: Tag question 'innit' (isn't it) used after most statements in MLE
'have got' over 'have' (I've got vs. I have)
Collective nouns take plural verbs (the team are vs. the team is)

rules: London Gen Z mixes MLE with Caribbean and Nigerian English markers — acknowledge multicultural roots.
Don't mix US slang into UK copy — feels American-pretending-British.

do_not_use: American spelling/slang in UK copy (color, awesome, gotten)
MLE/roadman slang for non-youth or luxury brands — wrong register
Stereotypical 'cor blimey' / 'old chap' — feels like American writing British

example_translations.note: Default casual is 'proper' + adjective. MLE markers only when audience fits.
